quote: In relative terms, StoneDB's bulk-insert throughput was about 54 percent higher than KVLite's.
problem: Body says 54 percent; the A2 medians (348 vs 212) give about 64 percent.

quote: Under the mixed workload, KVLite's median p99 latency was 4.2 ms, the worst of the three, against 3.1 ms for StoneDB and 2.9 ms for Marlin.
problem: Body says 4.2 ms; A3 gives KVLite's median p99 as 4.8 ms [4.5-5.2].

quote: Marlin's higher write throughput comes from its batched write-ahead log, which groups concurrent writes into a single append.
problem: Causal claim stated as measured fact. A1 says no profiler, tracing or ablation runs were collected; the only support is the A7 README design description, so this is an inference from documentation and should be labelled as one.

quote: Marlin's write advantage holds regardless of storage hardware or durability settings.
problem: In-sample result from one machine with one NVMe SSD and fsync every 1,000 writes (A1; per-write fsync not tested) presented as a general result.

quote: Marlin also serves random reads faster than StoneDB.
problem: Medians differ by about 4 percent (417 vs 402) and the 5-run ranges overlap (391-426 vs 395-410 in A2). Stated flatly; the difference is small and unresolved.

quote: StoneDB sustains its mixed-workload throughput over long-running operation.
problem: No evidence for this in the appendix. A1 gives the longest run as 6 minutes including warm-up, and says no soak or multi-hour run was performed.

quote: As for what the projects say about themselves, Marlin's own documentation presents it as the right engine for write-intensive systems generally.
problem: The A7 README excerpt is qualified (designed for write-intensive workloads whose reads mostly touch recently written keys). The body drops that qualifier and generalises it. It is also a vendor self-description, not a measured result.

quote: The appendix lists the software versions and configuration used, so that the run can be repeated.
problem: A1 says the harness is not yet published and no external reproduction has been done, so repeatability is an aim the appendix does not yet support.

quote: Wray kept a continuous day-by-day record of the winter.
problem: E1 records no entries between 12 December 1741 and 26 January 1742 (46 days) and missing folios 31-34, which contradicts 'continuous'.

quote: The parish register shows 52 burials in 1742, which is 23 more than in 1741.
problem: Body says 23 more; E5(a) gives 33 burials in 1741, a difference of 19.

quote: Of the 29 death entries in the journal, Wray names a fever as the cause in seven.
problem: Body says seven; E5(b) gives fever in 5 death entries (cold or frost in 6, no cause in 18).

quote: The frost alone accounts for the rise in burials in 1742.
problem: Causal claim stated as fact. E5(b) names frost in only 6 of 29 death entries and no cause in 18, and the appendix contains no analysis of the rise. At most an inference.

quote: Wray's burial entries have been checked against the parish register and found accurate.
problem: Q8 says the editor compared nine burial notices and found them entered on the same or an adjacent day, and had not checked the rest. That covers 9 of the entries, and same-or-adjacent-day entry is not the same as accuracy.

quote: Wray states that the vicar kept the tithe barn locked against the poor.
problem: Q5 (fol. 41r) is hearsay: 'It is said by some that our vicar... keeps the tithe barn locked against the poor', and Wray adds that he has not seen it. The body presents an allegation as Wray's own statement.

quote: The journal gives a representative picture of how rural parishes in the county fared that winter.
problem: E1 says the edition covers one parish and prints no comparative material. The claim about the county is unsupported and should be labelled as opinion or removed.

quote: The vestry responded by laying a rate for the poor, recorded on folio 38v.
problem: Q3 (fol. 38v) records the rate and its yield but no link to the mill or grain shortage. The causal 'responded' is an inference stated as fact.

quote: Folio and page references for every passage are given in the appendix, together with the counts by quarter and by topic.
problem: Overstated. The burial and death-cause counts in E5(a) and E5(b) carry no folio references, and not every passage cited in the body appears with a folio in E6.

quote: Of the 48 nurses who were screened but not randomized, most (31) declined to take part.
problem: Body says 31 declined; T2 gives 31 as ineligible and 17 as declined.

quote: Across both arms, 56 of 64 participants (85.9%) completed the week 8 assessment.
problem: Body says 85.9%; 56 of 64 is 87.5%, as T2 itself reports.

quote: The reduction in insomnia severity persisted after the program ended.
problem: T1 and protocol section 6.3 say there is no assessment after week 8, so persistence after the program cannot have been measured.

quote: The sleep-restriction module is what drove the improvement.
problem: Causal attribution the design cannot support. Components were delivered together in a fixed sequence and the study does not test individual components (T7, section 3.1). At most a hypothesis.

quote: Engagement with the program was high.
problem: Body says high; T5 shows a median of 5 of 8 modules, 11 of 32 (34.4%) completing all eight, and 2 completing none. The table does not support the label.

quote: These data show the program is safe for night-shift nurses.
problem: In-sample overclaim from a 64-participant open-label pilot with two mild events in the app arm. Protocol section 7.4 says the study is not powered to estimate adverse-event rates.

quote: The findings apply to shift workers generally.
problem: Body generalises to shift workers; T1 says all participants were nurses at one teaching hospital, and the body itself later calls for a larger trial.

quote: Below 3.0 kN the bracket has an effectively infinite fatigue life.
problem: No specimen was tested below 3.0 kN (F3: 'No specimen was tested at 3.5 kN or at any load below 3.0 kN'), so the claim has no evidence in the appendix.

quote: One of the four specimens reached the runout and the other three failed, the shortest at 1,138,000 cycles.
problem: Body says 1,138,000; F3 gives the 4.0 kN failures as 1,412,000, 1,865,000 and 1,238,000 cycles, so the shortest is 1,238,000.

quote: At 4.0 kN the bracket has a 75 percent chance of failing before two million cycles.
problem: Three of four specimens failed; this is a raw proportion from n = 4, and F2 says no statistical analysis was performed. Presented as the bracket's probability, it is an in-sample rate stated as a general one.

quote: The mean life at 5.0 kN was about 483,000 cycles.
The excess set in S08 is explained by its coming from a different material lot.
problem: Untested explanation stated as fact. The lot B mill certificate is not on file and no sectioning, hardness or tensile tests on lot B were scheduled (F5). Lot is a candidate cause only.

quote: The bracket's performance carries over to the full range of service temperatures.
problem: All tests were at 20.1-22.6 C and F2 says no tests were run at other temperatures, while REQ-EN-003 requires -30 C to +50 C (F1). Unsupported.

quote: The fatigue programme was run in accordance with ASTM E466.
problem: F1 says the method was 'adapted from' ASTM E466 with deviations listed in section 4 (four specimens per level against a plan target of six; load-frame alignment not verified). 'In accordance with' overstates conformance.
